item.title: Tené buena memoria, sobre todo si eres mentiroso.
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Keep your story straight; every new audience needs the same script.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Tené buena memoria, sobre todo si eres mentiroso."
❓ A liar does not get to tell one story and walk away. Each retelling has to match the last version, or someone will notice the slip. You use this saying when a coworker gives HR one timeline, the client another, and their group chat a third, then sweats trying to remember which detail went where.
AND: It is the nervous flip through a notebook you picture when a friend has to reconstruct a lie on the spot. You hear it after someone asks, "Wait, didn't you say Tuesday?" and the speaker freezes long enough for everyone to hear the gears grinding.
🔤 IN ENGLISH: • Have a good memory, especially if you are a liar. • Who remembers which version they told you? • If you're going to lie, have a good memory

item.title: Grace Under Pressure
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: The ministry calls a crocodile’s total lack of remorse grace under pressure. Asking where the bridge went can wait; interrupting lunch would be uncivil.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Grace Under Pressure"
❓ The clerks read zero remorse as steady nerves, so a bridge sold for scrap passes for composure. The ministry records calm and etiquette, while psychological fitness, accountability, and remorse never reach the agenda.
AND: The crocodile eats lunch in the rubble of the bridge he sold for scrap, napkin in his collar. Ants carry forms across the wreckage because the stamps still wait on the far side. One frog asks why he sold it; the other says not during lunch, that would be uncivil. The minutes log a steady hand. The afternoon agenda has no item about the bridge.

item.title: 🚽 Would you ask permission in a meeting if you had to go to the toilet?
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Over more than a decade, children learn to wait, comply, and accept a pecking order, so the same people will tolerate meetings, factory floors, and office desks later. That training also makes people more polite and less violent on the street, which is part of the domestication. One of the first casualties is learning: teachers reward compliance even when it does not help anyone understand the work.
item.sync:pageSocial:
🚽 Would you ask permission in a meeting if you had to go to the toilet?
At school, a child who needs the bathroom asks an adult first. The bell decides when children move. Teachers reward the child who waits quietly, and that posture later feels normal in meetings, factories, and office desks.
✜ School trains compliance apart from learning. A child can follow the schedule, sit still, and accept a grade without understanding the work. The system rewards the behavior that makes groups easy to manage.
✜ Factory managers saw the same problem before mass schooling had reached every worker. Cotton-mill doffers did the same job on the same machines in 1910, yet productivity varied sixfold. In some regions, one worker tended six machines. In others, a worker tended one. Managers blamed workers who resisted direct orders, arrived late, or refused tasks that clashed with status.
✜ School also teaches people to see rank as fair. Most fifth graders still want equal shares. By late adolescence, most prefer to divide rewards according to individual achievement.
The benefits are real. Schools can teach manners, cooperation, and quieter ways to settle conflict. They can also train people to submit to a modern hierarchy, while curiosity pays the bill.

item.title: El que tapa la olla también se quema.
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: You help hide the mess, then find yourself standing over the heat.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"El que tapa la olla también se quema."
❓ The lid looks like protection until the steam reaches the hand holding it down. You use this saying when someone helps hide a fault and ends up paying for the consequences too: a junior lies to a manager about a senior's missed deadline, then gets written up when the story breaks.
AND: It is the wary shrug you give a friend who volunteers to cover someone else's mess. A coworker deletes the warning email, smooths over a missed payment, or tells the client that the delay is under control. When the pot boils over, the person who kept the lid on is standing closest to the steam.
🔤 IN ENGLISH: • If you play with fire, you'll get burned • If you lie down with dogs, you get up with fleas • You reap what you sow

item.title: Bold Vision
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: The leader declares gravity optional for loyal citizens. The ministry does not question his contact with reality; it schedules a workshop on footnote typography and forgets to call the psychiatrist.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Bold Vision"
❓ The leader declares gravity optional for loyal citizens. The ministry does not question his contact with reality; it schedules a workshop on footnote typography and forgets to call the psychiatrist.
AND: At the podium he announces a law that physics politely refuses to obey. The ants reach for a thesaurus and call the moment ambition. Frog clerks open an implementation binder and argue about Arial versus the new national serif. Compliance wants a timeline; procurement wants a vendor; communications wants a tagline. Nobody asks whether the words describe the world.

item.title: La mona, aunque se vista de seda, mona se queda.
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Every year a new venture, and still nobody has been paid back.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"La mona, aunque se vista de seda, mona se queda."
❓ It describes people who want to pretend they are something they are not. They put on the silk, try and try and try, and they are still the same old monkey. A coworker shows up with a new car, then tailored suits, then a new title, and still hands the real work to the interns. When a deadline slips, the intern stays late and takes the client's complaint while the coworker collects the credit.
AND: It is the tired shrug of someone who has watched the same person try again and again and come out unchanged. You say it about the cousin who announces a new venture every year and has never paid anyone back. Nobody argues, because everyone has already seen the last three versions.
🔤 IN ENGLISH: • All hat and no cattle • Lipstick on a pig • You can't make a silk purse out of a sow's ear

item.title: A single label is a ceiling rather than a map
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: A clinic can close a child’s file after one diagnosis and never screen for movement, language, or injury history. Schools often plan around a single label while the child’s other struggles stay off the referral. Teachers can run a full year on one box that covers only part of what the child needs.
item.sync:pageSocial:
A single label is a ceiling rather than a map
A clinician says one word at the school gate, and the relief in the room makes everyone stop asking what else the child struggles with. The teacher plans the term around attention while movement, speech, and sleep never make it onto the form.
✜ Clinics often match symptoms to one checklist and treat that word as the whole profile. UK NICE expects autism assessments to cover coexisting conditions and motor problems, yet many files still close after the first label that fits.
✜ Local agencies run support in sequence. Funding and referrals attach to the paper that arrived, so a pupil with a language gap and an attention label may get help for focus alone while the next door stays shut for months.
✜ UK research puts developmental language disorder around one child in thirteen, and mainstream schools often steer more support toward autism than toward language needs at the same severity.
✜ Clinicians who skip head injury history often match focus problems to ADHD while a past injury stays off the chart. NICE treats acquired brain injury as part of that same assessment picture.
✜ The child waiting outside the head teacher's office pays for that one-label model every day. Parents can ask which movement screen and head injury history ran before the label landed. They can also ask the school for one everyday fix, a pencil grip or a seat near the door, while the second check waits.
The word sets the ceiling for what staff will measure. The child still walks in with every gap the first screen skipped.
